key_facts: Plaintiff has an established prior employment history with Randstad. Defendant Randstad US, LLC (operating as Randstad General Staffing and, within client facilities, as Randstad Inhouse Services) is a Delaware LLC and the primary Randstad operating entity for general staffing placements in California; 'Randstad General Staffing' and 'Randstad Inhouse Services' are trade names and division brands, not separate legal entities. Defendant RK Logistics Group, Inc. is a California corporation (incorporated April 23, 2004, HQ: 47020 Kato Road, Fremont, CA 94538) — a 3PL company specializing in semiconductor, EV, and high-tech logistics with multiple Bay Area facilities. Randstad Inhouse Services embeds a dedicated site manager within the RK Logistics facility. On June 30, 2026, Plaintiff submitted an employment application via the Indeed platform for the position of 'Class C Driver - Bobtail (Mon-Fri 2:30pm-11:00pm)' listed by RK Logistics Group, Inc. at its Newark, CA facility. RK Logistics sent Plaintiff an automated SMS acknowledgment at 8:26 PM on June 30 from +1 (762) 795-5146: 'Thanks for your interest in RK Logistics Group, Inc jobs.' The following morning, July 1, 2026 at 8:08 AM, Randstad recruiter Dishon Bryant texted Plaintiff from +1 (609) 901-1636: 'Hi Brendan, This is Dishon with Randstad. I'm contacting you regarding the class C driver position you applied for at RK Logistics. Give me a call when you get a chance.' This message establishes the direct nexus between Plaintiff's Indeed application and Randstad's inhouse staffing pipeline: Randstad's outreach came within approximately 12 hours of the Indeed application. On July 2, 2026, Dishon Bryant followed up by text, providing the identity and contact number of the embedded RK Logistics site manager: 'Site Manger / Danyea Watkins -5106955468' — the same Danyea Watkins (danyea.watkins@randstadusa.com; 510-695-5468) who, five days later, emailed Plaintiff the MVR form confirming the CDL commercial driving placement. The Bryant-to-Watkins text chain documents the complete pre-onboarding pipeline: Plaintiff's June 30 Indeed application to RK Logistics triggered Randstad's recruiter outreach within hours; Randstad then referred Plaintiff to the embedded RK Logistics site manager; and five days later the site manager completed onboarding with the MVR form. On July 7, 2026, Randstad sent Plaintiff a formal notification: 'Your employee status has changed to Rehired' — re-onboarding him into Randstad's operations with self-service portal access at workplace.randstad.com and weekly paycheck processing. That same afternoon, at 2:45 PM, RIS Site Manager II Danyea Watkins (danyea.watkins@randstadusa.com; 510-695-5468) — operating inside the RK Logistics Fremont facility — emailed Plaintiff requesting completion of an MVR (Motor Vehicle Record) form, confirming Plaintiff was being placed in a CDL commercial driving role. At 6:22 PM on July 7, 2026, Randstad submitted a background check request through vendor InfoMart LLC (Order No. 15780719) for the 'Randstad App' placement. The InfoMart report header confirms: Billing Code: RK LOGISTICS; Business Unit: RIS RK Logistics Fremont; Client Package: RK Logistics — establishing that RK Logistics is the billing client, configured the screening package criteria, and is the decision-making entity for the placement. The report's Decision Date is July 13, 2026 and its overall status is 'NEEDS APPROVAL, PER CLIENT CRITERIA.' On July 13, 2026 at 1:31 PM, InfoMart sent Plaintiff a 'Notice to Consumer for Employment Purposes' pursuant to FCRA §607(b) (15 U.S.C. §1681e(b)), informing him that InfoMart is 'reporting criminal or other public record information that may be adverse' to Randstad; dispute address: P.O. Box 2209, Alpharetta, GA 30023. The InfoMart report itself — now in Plaintiff's possession — confirms: (1) criminal history searched across seven jurisdictions: Fresno County CA, San Joaquin County CA, Santa Clara County CA, Stanislaus County CA, Clark County NV, State of New York, and Sheridan County WY — all returned 'No Record'; (2) federal criminal history (National Federal): 'No Record'; (3) OFAC Watch List: 'No name match found'; (4) OIG Exclusions List: 'not found'; (5) GSA Procurement Exclusion: 'not found'; (6) National Criminal Search / Sex Offender: 'Information Found' — jurisdiction: County: Sex Offender, State: California — Result: 'Record' — Name on file: Newanforbi, Brendan Ngehsi — and the report's conclusion: 'Subject is a registered Sex Offender in California.' The California Sex Offender Registry is therefore confirmed as the sole basis for the 'NEEDS APPROVAL' flag. This is not a case pled on information and belief — Plaintiff now holds the actual InfoMart report showing every criminal search returned clear, with the registry listing as the only adverse item. Penal Code § 290.46(j)(2)(E) categorically prohibits the use of registry information 'for purposes relating to ... Employment.' No exception applies to a CDL commercial driving placement. Under FCRA, Randstad may not take final adverse action until at least five business days after the July 13, 2026 pre-adverse notice — making the earliest compliant adverse action date July 21, 2026. On July 15, 2026, Randstad terminated Plaintiff's employment — only two business days after the July 13 pre-adverse notice, four days short of the five-business-day FCRA waiting period, and before the InfoMart 'NEEDS APPROVAL, PER CLIENT CRITERIA' flag was ever resolved to a final adverse determination by RK Logistics. On July 20, 2026, Plaintiff sent Pre-Filing Demand Letters to both Randstad (privacyofficer@randstad.com, cc: call.center@, rus-privacy@, hrsupport@, complianceofficer@randstadusa.com) and RK Logistics Group, Inc. (info@rklogisticsgroup.com, cc: peter.odonnell@, nikki.michaux@rklogisticsgroup.com), each demanding $85,000 in settlement with a response deadline of 5:00 PM Pacific Time on August 2, 2026, transmitting as an exhibit a verified Complaint for Damages executed the same day naming both entities and DOES 1-20, filed for Alameda Superior Court (venue proper under CCP §§395(a), 395.5 — the RK Logistics Fremont facility where Plaintiff was assigned and where the adverse decision was made and implemented). This is the fifth matter in the portfolio asserting PC §290.46(j) violations by an employer using registry information for employment purposes (Matters 22, 25, 26, 27 — Matter 23 is excluded from this count because Macy's completed the hire without any adverse action; see Matter 23).

Randstad terminated July 15, 2026 — two business days after the pre-adverse notice, short of FCRA's five-business-day wait. Demands July 20 ($85,000 each); complaint e-filed same day in Alameda Sup. Ct. (summons initially rejected for caption mismatch, corrected and accepted July 21). CMC Dec. 17, 2026. RK Logistics denied July 21 (employer-status + MVR grounds — answered in risk). damages: Statutory civil remedy under PC § 290.46(j)(4)(A): actual damages or $25,000, whichever is greater, plus attorney fees, for each unlawful use of registry information. CONSERVATIVE: ~$45,000 (statutory minimum plus modest emotional distress; Plaintiff was re-onboarded but had not yet commenced active paid shifts before the anticipated adverse action, so lost-wage recovery tracks the failure-to-hire posture of Matters 25 and 26 unless wages were actually earned during the July 7–adverse-action window). MODERATE: ~$110,000 (statutory penalty; ICRAA statutory plus punitive for willful noncompliance; emotional distress; fee-shifting under §290.46(j)(4)(A); if even one paid shift was worked, Tameny wrongful-termination damages add a meaningful lost-wages increment at CDL commercial-driving rates). AGGRESSIVE: ~$250,000 (aggregation across all six causes of action; punitive damages under Civ. Code §3294 multiplied by the portfolio-wide pattern of violations across five separate employers; if the CDL placement was operative and Plaintiff worked shifts, ongoing lost wage loss at CDL rates adds significantly; RK Logistics named as co-defendant adds end-client liability and creates cross-pressure between Randstad and RK Logistics, each incentivized to attribute the placement decision to the other).
risk: Extremely favorable — this is no longer an information-and-belief case. Plaintiff holds the actual InfoMart background check report (Order No. 15780719). The report conclusively shows: (1) every criminal court search (7 county/state jurisdictions) returned 'No Record'; federal criminal, OFAC, OIG, and GSA all clear; (2) the one and only flagged item is the National Sex Offender Search result — 'Subject is a registered Sex Offender in California'; (3) the overall report status is 'NEEDS APPROVAL, PER CLIENT CRITERIA' — not a flat rejection by InfoMart, but a flag sent to RK Logistics for its decision. This places the adverse decision squarely with RK Logistics and Randstad. The InfoMart report header makes RK Logistics' role undeniable: Billing Code 'RK LOGISTICS,' Business Unit 'RIS RK Logistics Fremont,' Client Package 'RK Logistics' — RK Logistics configured the screening criteria that triggered the 'NEEDS APPROVAL' flag. PC §290.46(j)(2)(E) is a categorical prohibition applicable to all employment purposes regardless of position or employer type; no 'protect a person at risk' exception could plausibly apply to a CDL commercial truck-driving placement. The InfoMart report itself contains the required California ICRA notice (Civ. Code §1786.26) and the FCRA Summary of Rights — confirming that InfoMart and Randstad/RK Logistics are on notice of the statutory framework. The two-defendant structure (Randstad as employer of record + RK Logistics as the criteria-setting end client) creates joint-and-several liability and cross-defendant settlement pressure: each party will be incentivized to attribute the adverse action decision to the other, potentially generating additional admissions. No qualified immunity available (state law, private employers). This matter is now evidentiary comparably to Matter 22 (Pilot), where the post-adverse action notice was the smoking gun — here the BGC report itself serves that role because it proves the registry hit and that every other search was clear. On July 21, 2026, RK Logistics responded to the pre-filing demand denying liability on two grounds. The first — that Randstad, not RK Logistics, was Plaintiff's employer — threatens only the Tameny wrongful-termination claim, which requires an employer-employee relationship; it does not reach the other five causes of action, none of which turn on formal employer status the same way. It is also in tension with RK Logistics' own Transportation Manager, Jack Altares, who wrote on July 15, 2026 that 'Brendan's MVR came back and unfortunately, we will not be able to move forward with him as a driver for RK' — RK Logistics personnel making the substantive placement decision, cutting against the letter's claim that RK Logistics 'did not and could not' act as an employer. The second ground — that the rejection was MVR-based, not registry-based — initially appeared serious: RK Logistics attached a SambaSafety report showing a commercial (Class A) disqualification for refusing a CMV chemical test (eff. 12/1/2024) and a related suspension (eff. 2/20/2025, cleared 5/19/2026). On review, both entries attach to Plaintiff's commercial driving privileges, not the non-commercial Class C license the RK Logistics 'Class C Driver' posting required; Plaintiff holds documentation of a Class C license reissue dated June 11, 2026 — three weeks after the suspension cleared and five weeks before he applied to RK Logistics — which the SambaSafety report's own 'PENDING APPLICATION' notation is consistent with. As between the two named defendants, Randstad's exposure remains the more direct and is not reduced by RK Logistics' response: Randstad ordered the InfoMart background check, received the pre-adverse notice, and delivered the July 15 termination — two business days after the pre-adverse notice, short of FCRA's five-business-day waiting period — and has no employer-status defense available to it at all.
